sections.heading: Your duties as a sponsor
sections.text:
When you hold a sponsor licence, the Home Office expects you to:
- Carry out and keep right to work checks for every employee, not just sponsored workers
- Keep the records set out in Appendix D of the sponsor guidance for each sponsored worker
- Report certain changes through the Sponsor Management System, usually within 10 working days, such as a worker not starting, leaving, taking long unpaid absence, or a change to their job, salary or work location
- Pay sponsored workers at least the salary on their Certificate of Sponsorship, and make sure the role is genuine
- Not pass sponsorship costs, such as the licence fee, Certificate of Sponsorship or Immigration Skills Charge, on to workers
- Keep your Key Personnel and business details up to date

sections.heading: Home Office compliance visits
sections.text: The Home Office can visit sponsors before or after granting a licence, and visits can be unannounced. Officers usually check your HR records, interview Key Personnel and sometimes speak to sponsored workers. They look at whether your records are complete, whether reporting has been done on time, and whether each sponsored role matches what was stated on the Certificate of Sponsorship.

sections.heading: What happens if you are not compliant?
sections.text:
If the Home Office finds problems, it can:
- Downgrade your licence to a B rating, with an action plan you must follow and pay for
- Suspend your licence while it investigates
- Revoke your licence, which usually means your sponsored workers' permission is cut short, typically to 60 days, unless they find another sponsor

Employing someone without the right to work can also lead to a civil penalty of up to £60,000 per illegal worker.

faqs.q: What is a sponsor licence compliance audit?
faqs.a: A review of your HR records and processes against the Home Office sponsor guidance, carried out the way a compliance officer would. You get a report of any gaps and how to fix them.

faqs.q: How quickly must sponsors report changes?
faqs.a: Most changes, such as a sponsored worker leaving or a change to their role or salary, must be reported on the Sponsor Management System within 10 working days.

faqs.q: Can the Home Office visit without warning?
faqs.a: Yes. Compliance visits can be unannounced, so your records need to be up to date at all times.

faqs.q: What happens to sponsored workers if a licence is revoked?
faqs.a: Their permission to stay is usually cut short, typically to 60 days, unless they find a new sponsor or another way to stay.
